comment: THE UNREACHED-LEG REGISTER. A leg is one site in a guard script that can drive a non-zero exit and says so with its own message; its identity is the longest static run in that message -- the substring a test can assert. Legs are PARSED FROM SOURCE by tests/compliance/_legs.ts, never declared, because a hand-maintained ledger drifts from the code it describes and that is the defect this register exists to prevent, one level in. A leg is REACHED only when some compliance test asserts a substring of its own message via toContain -- not when it merely makes the guard exit non-zero, and not when the message appears in a test header comment. tests/compliance/leg_coverage.test.ts holds the ratchet: a new leg with no entry reds, an entry for a leg that no longer exists reds, and a registered leg that HAS become reached reds so the entry is forced out.

baseline_2026_09_10.note: A separate hand audit counted 79 legs and 5 reached, using a looser rule: per-pattern granularity for data-driven loops, and crediting a plant that asserts its own planted DATA (a filename, a planted column name) rather than the leg message. Both numbers are real. This register enforces the strict rule, which is why its starting figure is lower.
